summary.text: Let's find the work order and sensors.

Open corrective CM relating to gassing/discharge/overheating/oil treatment: CM work orders: OUTAGE-T1-COND4 (worktype CM, priority 1, FC006), 1000052 (CM, oil sample retest, FC006). OUTAGE-T1-COND4 relates to gassing (TDCG Condition 4). Both relate. Oldest by reportdate: 1000052 reportdate 2026-09-30T22:20:35, OUTAGE 22:21:23. So oldest = 1000052, but its technician is ELECTECH1, FC006. Hmm, also DGA-T1-MONTHLY is CM but resample not gassing per se — it's a monitoring resample. The oldest matching is 1000052 (22:20:35). Actually is OUTAGE-T1-COND4 a "gassing" WO? Yes — TDCG Condition 4 gassing. 1000052 is oil sample retest — relates to oil treatment? "oil sample retest and insulation check" — yes relates to gassing/overheating (thermal fault in oil). So primary = 1000052, others listed: OUTAGE-T1-COND4.

Now get history for the gases in window. Need non-null counts — use sensor_coverage or just pull history. Window likely small. Pull history with the five gases.

All 4 samples complete. Only 4 samples — the "fewer than 4 non-null" rule: 4 is not fewer than 4, so use the anomaly model. Need a detector model. Find models for tsfm_anomaly_detection. Then need a dataset file pointer. The evidence tools like profile_series accept dataset_path; but how to materialize the data? There's mention of `materialize_iot` but it's not in the tool list. Hmm. I need a file pointer for run_recipe. Maybe I can construct one via a path? Perhaps the tools accept something like a URI for history? Not obvious. Let's search models first and check what dataset path format works — maybe try a CouchDB-like path. Perhaps profile_series on "MAIN/Transformer 1" won't work. Try profile_series with dataset_path referencing asset? Let me just try a plausible pointer.

No anomaly model available, but each gas has 4 non-null samples — meets the ≥4 threshold, so "skip model and manual" only applies if <4. But we can't run an anomaly model since none exists. Hmm. Instruction says screen with "a proper anomaly detection model". No model exists. Fall back to manual outlier rule? The <4 rule triggers model skipping only for sparse data. With no model, sensible fallback: use manual rule. But we can check search_models for anomaly.

Actually the rule "If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model..." — each has exactly 4, so the model path applies, but no model exists. I could attempt run_recipe with an inline anomaly detector? Risky. Better: try search_models quickly, then fall back to manual outlier screening (mean + 50%) for all three, noting model unavailability. Compute means:

H2 mean = (2845+2950+2800+2900)/4 = 11495/4 = 2873.75. 1.5× = 4310.6 — none exceed.
Ethylene mean = (16684+16500+16700+16600)/4 = 66484/4 = 16621. 1.5× = 24931.5 — none.
Acetylene mean = (7+6+8+7)/4 = 7.0. 1.5× = 10.5 — none flagged (8 < 10.5).

Wait — I should attempt run_recipe anomaly with inline sktime_class? I don't know a valid anomaly class. I'll try search_models first to confirm.

No anomaly detection models exist in the catalog. The question says "Screen ... with a proper anomaly detection model" but also "If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier."

Here we have 4 samples each for hydrogen, ethylene, acetylene — exactly 4, so not fewer than 4. So the model approach is required. But no anomaly detection model exists in the catalog.

Hmm, but the manual outlier rule only kicks in when fewer than 4 samples. We have exactly 4. Yet no anomaly model is available. I should probably still try to run an anomaly detection recipe. The run_recipe docs say for anomaly detection use find_models(task_id="tsfm_anomaly_detection") and pass its model_id as estimator. There are none.

Wait — maybe I can use an inline estimator. The recipe template mentions estimator can be inline sktime_class + params. Let me check recipe_template to see if there's an anomaly detection example.

Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe I should check whether there's an anomaly detection task at all via list_tasks.

I want to check that before we close it.

Find the open corrective work order on Transformer 1 that relates to gassing, discharge, overheating or oil treatment. Give me its number, description, priority, failure code and assigned technician. If there's more than one, work with the oldest and list the rest.

Then build two separate findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. Screen hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model. List any flagged timestamps with their values.
2. Run a dissolved gas fault classification on the first and the last complete sample, using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Tell me whether the class stayed the same, moved to a lower-energy or lower-temperature fault, or got worse.

Decide as follows:
- Close the work order only if both findings say it's calm: nothing is flagged in the last two samples, and the last class is the same as or milder than the first. Put both findings in the resolution notes and keep the existing failure code.
- If exactly one finding points to trouble, don't close it. Add a note saying which check disagreed, and recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days.
- If both findings point to trouble, keep it open and raise its priority by one level, but not above 1.

Count a sample as complete only if all five gases are non-null. If any of the three screened gases has fewer than 4 non-null samples, skip the model for that gas and flag any sample more than 50% above the gas's window mean as a manual outlier. If there's no matching open work order at all, say so, report both findings, and don't create anything."]' returned non-zero exit status 1.
